texts.preamble: Hemraj Chauhan vs Ravi (11909 Jaitpur) on 31 August, 2023 :1: In The Court Sh. Naveen Kumar Kashyap Additional District And Sessions Judge Po Mact, South East District, Saket Courts: New Delhi
texts.facts: In this case, originally a claim petition was filed by the claimant u/s 166 (1) MV Act. 2. As per the case of claimant, in brief, it is stated that on 27.06.2009, original claimant/ injured Hemraj Chauhan (since deceased) was coming on his motorcycle bearing no. HR 50A 8060 from Greater Kailash to his home via Agra canal Road, Suddenly Maruti van no. DID 2008 came at a very high speed from wrong side towards gas Godam, Agra Canal Road, driven by R-1 in a rash and negligent manner and in contravention of traffic rules and hit the said motorcycle of the injured with great force. Due to such impact, injured fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries including multiple fractures. Claimant was taken to Holy Family Hospital and Thereafter Admitted in Apollo Hospital, New Delhi. 3. Further, as per record, a DAR is also filed at relevant time MACT No.: 3954/16 Hemraj Chauhan Vs. Ravi Pratap Singh & Ors. Page No. 2 of 24 rpt :3: by the concerned police official. 4. Further as per record, FIR in question on. 119/2009 u/s 279, 338 r/w 146/196 MV Act and 468/471 IPC was also registered and charge sheet was also filed u/s 279, 338 IPC. 5. Further as per record, R-1/ driver / Ravi Pratap Singh appeared on 04.12.2009 along with Ld. Counsel but thereafter, stopped appearing. Further, he did not file any reply. 6. Further as per record, R-2/ registered owner Gurucharan Singh S/o Ratan Singh appeared and also filed his reply. In nutshell, it is stated by R-2 that he is wrongly impleaded in the present case as he already sold the vehicle to R-3 on 24.03.2008 and even possession was handed over to R-3. Even otherwise, it is stated that as such, R-2 was not the owner at the time of accident nor R-1 is the employee of R-2. 7. Further, R-3/ alleged possession holder Harish Kumar also appeared and filed his reply. In nutshell, it is stated by R-3 in his reply dated 12.04.2012 that he is neither the owner nor the driver of the offending vehicle in question as such his name be deleted. It is further stated that no fault is in his part. 8. In this case, there was no third party insurance of such Hemraj Chauhan vs Ravi (11909 Jaitpur) on 31 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67363530/ 2 offending vehicle. 9. From the material on record, the following issues were framed on 11.07.2012 by my Ld. Whether the petitioner received grievous injuries in the road traffic accident which took place at about 10.00 PM on 27.06.2009 involving Maruti Van bearing no. DID 2008 due to rash and negligent driving of R-1 and owned by R-2 & R-3? OPP 2. Page No. 3 of 24 rp :4: petitioner is entitled to claim and from whom? OPP 3. Relief. 10. further as per record, despite opportunity given, claimant failed to lead RE and thereafter even stopped appearing as such, vide order dated 25.02.2015, the present claim petition was dismissed for non appearance. File was consigned to record room. 11. Further, as per record, thereafter, after about 4 years on 07.01.2019, an application filed by claimant Hemraj Chauhan for restoration of the case. Ultimately vide order dated 16.03.2021, passed by my Ld Predecessor, present case was restored to its original position subject to certain condition. 12. Thereafter, matter was put up for PE. 13. Ultimately as per record on 23.03.2022 only, the original claimant/ injured Hemraj Chauhan filed his examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents Ex. PW-1/1 to Ex.PW-1/10 and mark A to mark M including OPD cards, DAR, medical bills, MLC of concerned hospital. As per record, despite opportunity such witness was not cross-examined by respondent side. 14. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 15. Further as per record, no RE led by respondents side and their RE was closed. In fact, respondent stopped participating in present proceeding by such stage. 16. Further as per record, at the final stage, the original claimant expired and on application moved, his legal heirs/ wife/ Smt. Savita and major son / Kuldeep Chauhan were substituted MACT No.: 3954/16 Hemraj Chauhan Vs. Ravi Pratap Singh & Ors. Page No. 4 of 24 rpt as LRs as claimants in the present claim petition. 17. Arguments were addressed by counsel for petitioner, But despite opportunity given, respondent side failed to address any arguments. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. 20. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal.
texts.arguments: In Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 21. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held MACT No.: 3954/16 Hemraj Chauhan Vs. Ravi Pratap Singh & Ors. Page No. 5 of 24 rpt that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. Page No. 6 of 24 rpt decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for Hemraj Chauhan vs Ravi (11909 Jaitpur) on 31 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67363530/ 4 short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent MACT No.: 3954/16 Hemraj Chauhan Vs. Ravi Pratap Singh & Ors. 26.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 26.7.
